newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Southern unit mandates banks for CEPA loan.
newsitem.headline: Southern unit mandates banks for CEPA loan.

text.p: Southern Energy Asia has mandated BA Asia, Fuji Bank and Citicorp International to arrange a US$850 million term loan facility, bankers said.
The borrower is wholly owned by Southern Co unit Southern Energy Inc.
Bankers said the non-recourse financing facility has a final maturity of five years. Repayment is in bullet form.
Pricing details are not yet available.
Proceeds will be used to partially finance the company's proposed acquisition of Hopewell Holdings unit Consolidated Electric Power Asia (CEPA).
The loan has been fully underwritten, bankers noted.
Hopewell Holdings agreed in October to sell a majority stake in CEPA to Southern Co in a deal worth US$2.7 billion.
Under the agreement, CEPA shareholders will receive US$2.1 billion from Southern and US$600 million in dividends for 80 percent of the company.
In addition to the loan financing, Southern is expected to put up about US$1.2 billion in cash.
